page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 server family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs and 2 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1 GB per core. The underlying hardware features a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. This single physical core supports hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography, and BMI2. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2-highcpu-2 demonstrates performance characteristics that fall into the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU benchmark scored 1399.29, placing it in the bottom 25%, while the multi-core score of 1841.88 ranks in the bottom 10%. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 13.72 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 11.78 GB/sec, both falling in the bottom 10%. Computational tasks such as Geekbench software compilation (1719.0) and ray tracing (1357.0) also rank in the bottom 10%. For lightweight language model tasks, the instance achieves 116.03 tokens per second for prompt processing and 34.34 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated compute resources, but presents a clear tradeoff in memory capacity and overall performance density. The limited 2 GB of RAM restricts its utility for memory-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight, compute-focused workloads with minimal memory footprints, such as basic single-threaded processing, simple microservices, small-scale utility scripting, or development and testing environments that do not require high memory or storage throughput.
